headline: Count ordered sequences by their final value
statement: Count ordered sequences of numbers from nums whose sum equals target. Values may be reused, and different orders count separately. nums contains distinct positive integers.
constraints: The answer fits a signed 32-bit integer
intuition: For any sequence totaling total, its final value is some value in nums; removing that final value leaves a sequence totaling total-value. Add these disjoint possibilities. Process totals outside and values inside so order is counted.
approach: Set dp[0] to one for the empty sequence.
For each total from one to target, sum dp[total-value] for usable values.
correctness: Every counted sequence has exactly one final value and one preceding sequence. The recurrence therefore counts each ordered sequence exactly once. Positive values make every dependency a smaller total, so the bottom-up order is valid.
bruteForce: Recursively construct every possible ordered sequence; without memoization identical remaining totals are recomputed exponentially.

complexity.explanation: Each target sum considers every possible final value once.

pitfalls: Loop order differs from counting unordered coin combinations.
dp[0]=1 is required to count one-element sequences.
Zero or negative numbers would invalidate finite acyclic counting and are excluded.

Only the final answer is guaranteed to fit signed 32-bit storage. Some intermediate reachable totals may have larger counts when the final target is unreachable; Python integers handle these automatically.
